question: A facility submits its monthly NHMIS report late, on the twentieth day of the following month. What is the immediate consequence of this delay?

options.A: It automatically cancels all vaccine deliveries for the clinic.
options.B: It erases all electronic records stored on the server.
options.C: It requires the midwife in charge to pay a cash fine.
options.D: It holds up regional collation and delays national health planning.

explanation: Late facility reports break the timeline for LGA and state compilation, delaying the entire country's health data updates. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T4#BMP316_U1_T4_h3)

question: What is the primary purpose of data validation at the health facility level?

options.A: To check for mathematical errors and missing entries before submission
options.B: To calculate the exact revenue generated from user fees
options.C: To decide which members of staff deserve a promotion
options.D: To rewrite old patient case notes into a digital format

explanation: Validation catches mistakes like wrong tally totals or omitted information so incorrect data does not enter the official database. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T4#BMP316_U1_T4_h4)

question: Why should facility staff hold internal review meetings before sending their monthly reports?

options.A: To train new security guards on basic record keeping.
options.B: To spot discrepancies and resolve inconsistencies together.
options.C: To celebrate the end of another stressful working month.
options.D: To dispose of old paper registers by burning them safely.

explanation: Team reviews allow colleagues to cross-check numbers and fix mistakes before the report leaves the clinic doors. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T4#BMP316_U1_T4_h4)

question: What is the name of the primary electronic software platform used for health data reporting in Nigeria?

options.A: Primary Health Care Tracking Application
options.B: National Electronic Medical Record Database
options.C: Nigerian Midwifery and Nursing Portal
options.D: District Health Information Software version 2 (DHIS2)

explanation: DHIS2 is the web-based software platform utilized nationwide for entering, storing, and analyzing routine health management information. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T4#BMP316_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which challenge frequently disrupts electronic data uploading in many rural primary health care clinics across Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive speed of the local computer networks
options.B: A complete lack of any patient attendance registers
options.C: Unreliable internet connectivity and frequent power outages
options.D: Strict government bans on digital computers in clinics

explanation: Poor electricity and weak network signals make direct digital uploading difficult in remote areas, necessitating hybrid paper pathways. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T4#BMP316_U1_T4_h5)

question: How can a midwife best use facility immunization data to improve health outcomes in the local community?

options.A: By stopping all immunization services until numbers improve
options.B: By filing the numbers away neatly without looking at them again
options.C: By identifying drops in coverage and planning targeted outreach visits
options.D: By waiting for federal supervisors to point out the mistakes

explanation: Local data analysis helps midwives find communities with low coverage so they can deploy mobile outreach teams effectively. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T4#BMP316_U1_T4_h6)

question: A clinic register shows a sudden increase in malaria cases among pregnant women over two months. What immediate local action should the midwife take?

options.A: Wait until the annual national report is published next year
options.B: Close the antenatal clinic until the rainy season ends completely
options.C: Intensify malaria prevention education and check ITN distribution stocks
options.D: Transfer all pregnant women to hospitals in another state

explanation: Noticing trends in local data allows midwives to take immediate corrective action, such as promoting insecticide-treated nets and ensuring adequate treatment supplies. [learn more](BMP316_U1_T4#BMP316_U1_T4_h6)

question: What is the main purpose of a Primary Health Care (PHC) maternity unit in our communities?

options.A: Serving as a tertiary referral teaching hospital
options.B: Managing complex surgical obstetric complications
options.C: Providing first-contact maternal and child health services
options.D: Conducting advanced medical research on tropical diseases

explanation: PHC units are the closest point of entry for community healthcare, focusing on routine care and early detection of problems. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T1#BMP323_U1_T1_h1)

question: Why must a PHC maternity unit always be open and ready 24 hours a day?

options.A: Routine antenatal drugs are only dispensed during the night
options.B: Labour and delivery emergencies happen unexpectedly at any hour
options.C: Community members prefer night-time clinic visits for privacy
options.D: Government policy requires nurses to sleep inside the facility

explanation: Childbirth is unpredictable, making round-the-clock staffing essential for managing sudden complications like postpartum haemorrhage. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T1#BMP323_U1_T1_h1)

question: Which of these is NOT strictly needed to run a safe daily maternity unit?

options.A: Central air conditioning systems in every room
options.B: Continuous clean water supply for hand hygiene
options.C: Reliable backup lighting sources for night duties
options.D: Functional equipment like BP cuffs and fetoscopes

explanation: While ventilation is important, luxury cooling is not a life-saving operational standard, whereas water, light, and basic tools are mandatory. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T1#BMP323_U1_T1_h2)

question: A midwife starts her morning shift at a rural clinic and sees that the autoclave for sterilizing instruments is broken. What should she do first?

options.A: Advise all pregnant women in labor to walk to a tertiary hospital instead
options.B: Proceed with deliveries using unsterilized metal instruments to save time
options.C: Close the entire facility down permanently until a new machine is purchased
options.D: Arrange alternative sterilization methods or safe backups before conducting invasive procedures

explanation: Infection control cannot be bypassed; alternative methods like boiling or using backup sets must be arranged to maintain safety. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T1#BMP323_U1_T1_h2)

question: What is the biggest risk of having an unbalanced staff roster in a rural maternity unit?

options.A: Staff members will receive equal monthly salaries regardless of duty hours
options.B: Shifts may be left without an experienced skilled birth attendant during emergencies
options.C: Pregnant women will stop attending antenatal care on market days
options.D: The local government council will withhold the facility overhead budget

explanation: Every shift must contain competent personnel to handle sudden obstetric emergencies safely without delays. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T1#BMP323_U1_T1_h3)

question: How can training other health workers like Community Health Extension Workers (CHEWs) help a maternity unit?

options.A: By replacing the midwife completely during complicated surgical operations
options.B: By taking over administrative budget planning from the local government
options.C: By assisting with vital signs and routine preparation to support the midwife
options.D: By prescribing advanced specialist drugs without supervision

explanation: Delegating supporting tasks allows midwives to focus on clinical assessments and active management of labour. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T1#BMP323_U1_T1_h3)

question: What does the stock management rule FEFO stand for in a pharmacy store?

options.A: First-Expired, First-Out
options.B: Fast-Entry, Fast-Order
options.C: Free-Equipment, Free-Offer
options.D: Final-Evaluation, Final-Output

explanation: FEFO ensures that medicines expiring sooner are dispensed before newer stocks to prevent drug wastage. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T1#BMP323_U1_T1_h4)

question: Why is keeping the correct temperature critical when storing oxytocin at primary clinics?

options.A: Cold storage is only required to preserve the pleasant smell of the drug
options.B: Heat exposure destroys its potency, making it ineffective for preventing bleeding
options.C: Warm medicine causes severe allergic reactions in postpartum mothers
options.D: High temperatures turn liquid oxytocin into a solid tablet form

explanation: Oxytocin is a heat-sensitive peptide hormone that loses its efficacy if left outside cold chain storage, risking maternal hemorrhage. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T1#BMP323_U1_T1_h4)

question: What is known as the single most effective way to prevent the spread of infections in a clinic?

options.A: Spraying chemical disinfectants on patients
options.B: Regular and thorough hand hygiene
options.C: Sweeping the delivery floor four times daily
options.D: Wearing heavy rubber boots during shifts

explanation: Handwashing with soap and water or alcohol rub removes transient microorganisms and stops cross-contamination. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T1#BMP323_U1_T1_h5)

question: A midwife finishes delivering a baby and needs to dispose of blood-soaked gauze pads. Where should she put them?

options.A: Inside the general waste basket meant for paper and food wrappers
options.B: On top of the nurse's desk to dry out before final disposal
options.C: Into the box containing clean delivery gowns for the next patient
options.D: In the infectious waste bin designated for contaminated materials

explanation: Blood-contaminated items pose infection risks and must go into biohazard or infectious waste containers. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T1#BMP323_U1_T1_h5)

question: What key document must always go with a woman when transferring her from a PHC to a secondary hospital?

options.A: The original receipt for antenatal registration fees paid at the clinic
options.B: A personal letter of introduction written by the patient's husband
options.C: A signed consent form allowing surgical procedures at the tertiary center
options.D: A clear, written referral note detailing assessments and interventions

explanation: Receiving clinicians need to know what care has already been given and why the patient was transferred to act quickly. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T1#BMP323_U1_T1_h6)

question: Which of these conditions means a patient at a PHC needs an immediate referral to a higher hospital?

options.A: Signs of severe pre-eclampsia or eclampsia
options.B: Normal vertex delivery of a healthy term baby
options.C: Mild lower back pain during the third trimester
options.D: Request for routine tetanus toxoid vaccination

explanation: Severe pre-eclampsia and eclampsia carry high risks of maternal stroke or death, requiring higher-level facility management. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T1#BMP323_U1_T1_h6)

question: What is the main reason for filling out a partograph during active labour?

options.A: To record the personal contact addresses of relatives
options.B: To calculate the total revenue generated from clinic fees
options.C: To monitor labour progress and detect deviations early
options.D: To schedule the exact discharge time for the newborn

explanation: The partograph provides a pictorial overview of cervical dilation and fetal condition, flagging prolonged labor promptly. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T1#BMP323_U1_T1_h7)

question: Why are confidential maternal near-miss audits helpful for a maternity unit?

options.A: They automatically secure financial grants from international donors
options.B: They provide legal evidence to prosecute negligent family members in court
options.C: They uncover systemic problems by studying severe complications that women survived
options.D: They replace the need for writing daily entries in the delivery register

explanation: Near-miss cases offer rich lessons on healthcare system bottlenecks without the tragic finality of a maternal death. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T1#BMP323_U1_T1_h7)

question: What is your main role as a midwife when working with a community-led maternal survival project?

options.A: Taking full financial control of community funds
options.B: Reporting directly to international donor agencies
options.C: Replacing all traditional birth attendants entirely
options.D: Serving as a technical advisor to empower locals

explanation: Midwives guide and support the community rather than taking over leadership roles, ensuring local empowerment and sustainability. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T2#BMP323_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why do maternal health projects usually work better when they are led by the community itself?

options.A: Traditional birth attendants stop practicing medicine permanently
options.B: External organizations provide unlimited funding for all hospital bills
options.C: Local people directly address their specific cultural and geographic barriers
options.D: Rural health facilities are completely eliminated to save transport time

explanation: When initiatives are designed by the community, they target the exact local obstacles that keep women away from safe care. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T2#BMP323_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is the main reason for conducting a community diagnosis before starting a new health project?

options.A: Gathering local data to identify specific health barriers and needs
options.B: Fulfilling strict paperwork requirements for the federal ministry
options.C: Determining how much salary the visiting midwives will earn
options.D: Punishing traditional birth attendants who refuse to cooperate

explanation: A community diagnosis uncovers the exact local challenges, such as distance or cultural taboos, that need targeted solutions. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T2#BMP323_U1_T2_h2)

question: Why is it risky to rely only on national health averages when planning a local maternal program?

options.A: National averages hide severe local disparities and unique village challenges
options.B: Local primary health centres do not care about national statistics
options.C: Rural women refuse to answer questions based on national surveys
options.D: National data is always completely fabricated by international organizations

explanation: A country-wide average might look acceptable, but a single remote community might face extreme danger due to impassable roads. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T2#BMP323_U1_T2_h2)

question: Who is the most important group to involve first when introducing a rural maternal health program?

options.A: Traditional and community leaders
options.B: Foreign donor organization directors
options.C: International human rights lawyers
options.D: Federal pharmaceutical manufacturers

explanation: Community and traditional leaders hold the social influence necessary to encourage or discourage health-seeking behaviors among residents. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T2#BMP323_U1_T2_h3)

question: A village elder is hesitant to let pregnant women visit the clinic due to custom. What is best to do first?

options.A: Report him to the police for obstructing essential public health services
options.B: Threaten to cut off all government food supplies to his household
options.C: Ignore his authority completely and open the clinic doors anyway
options.D: Approach him respectfully to discuss the health risks and build a shared solution

explanation: Respectful dialogue builds trust and helps leaders see the project as a shared benefit rather than a challenge to their authority. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T2#BMP323_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the primary job of a Community Health Committee in maternal care programs?

options.A: Performing complex surgical operations during complicated deliveries
options.B: Acting as a bridge between villagers and health facility staff
options.C: Auditing international financial accounts across the entire country
options.D: Manufacturing essential drugs inside the local primary health centre

explanation: The committee connects the community with the health facility, ensuring local ownership and smooth problem-solving. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T2#BMP323_U1_T2_h4)

question: Why should a Community Health Committee include diverse members like market leaders and youth?

options.A: It prevents women from holding any leadership positions on the board
options.B: It guarantees that the government will pay high salaries to every member
options.C: It ensures all segments of the population feel included and represented
options.D: It stops elders from participating in village health decisions altogether

explanation: Inclusivity ensures that different social groups trust the committee and actively participate in health programs. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T2#BMP323_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is the most helpful way to work with traditional birth attendants in community programs?

options.A: Imposing heavy prison sentences for anyone who practices at home
options.B: Training them to recognize danger signs and promote early referral
options.C: Employing them as fully certified professional graduate midwives
options.D: Ignoring them completely until they close their traditional practices

explanation: Since many women still patronize TBAs, training them to spot danger signs saves lives by reducing referral delays. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T2#BMP323_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why do outright bans on traditional birth attendants often fail in rural areas?

options.A: Traditional attendants are legally permitted to perform cesarean sections
options.B: The government lacks enough prisons to hold all the traditional attendants
options.C: Women continue to visit them secretly due to cultural preference and proximity
options.D: Midwives are too few in number to care for any pregnant women at all

explanation: Outright bans drive practices underground, leading to dangerous home births without any oversight or safe referral linkage. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T2#BMP323_U1_T2_h5)

question: Which phase of the three delays model do emergency transport systems directly address?

options.A: The delay in moving from home to a health facility
options.B: The delay in deciding to seek medical care at home
options.C: The delay in receiving treatment inside the hospital
options.D: The delay in government budget release for health

explanation: Transport systems solve the physical barrier of moving a laboring woman from her remote village to a referral hospital. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T2#BMP323_U1_T2_h6)

question: Why must transport solutions match the specific geography of a local area?

options.A: A motorcycle is useless in riverine areas just as a boat cannot drive on dirt roads
options.B: Federal health laws forbid using tricycles as emergency medical ambulances
options.C: Rural women refuse to ride in any vehicle that does not have air conditioning
options.D: International donors refuse to fund vehicles unless they are imported from abroad

explanation: Different terrains require different modes of transport, such as boats for riverine zones or rugged motorcycles for hilly tracks. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T2#BMP323_U1_T2_h6)

question: What is a key sign that a community-led health initiative has achieved long-term success?

options.A: All traditional birth attendants leave the village to live in cities
options.B: The primary health centre stops keeping written medical registers
options.C: The international donor agency renews its multi-million dollar grant
options.D: The community finances its own upkeep without relying on external NGOs

explanation: True sustainability means the local people have taken full financial and operational ownership of their health programs. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T2#BMP323_U1_T2_h7)

question: Why is regularly reviewing clinic data useful for a community health team?

options.A: It prevents any pregnant woman from ever experiencing a complication
options.B: It proves to the federal government that the midwife is working hard
options.C: It helps the community spot ongoing problems and adjust their local strategies
options.D: It is required to pass international nursing council board examinations

explanation: Reviewing data lets the team see what is failing, such as high bleeding rates, so they can fix it immediately. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T2#BMP323_U1_T2_h7)

question: What is a major characteristic of a hard-to-reach community in healthcare terms?

options.A: Lacking easy access to standard health facilities
options.B: Being located inside major urban capital cities
options.C: Having too many private clinics operating at once
options.D: Refusing all forms of modern medicine completely

explanation: Hard-to-reach communities face physical, geographic, or financial barriers that prevent them from easily reaching established health centres. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T3#BMP323_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why must a midwife look beyond simple geographic distance when assessing a hard-to-reach population?

options.A: Government policy forbids looking at financial records
options.B: Maps are always completely accurate regarding travel times
options.C: Cultural beliefs and transport costs also block care access
options.D: Distance is the only factor that truly matters for health planning

explanation: Physical distance is only one part of the problem; financial constraints, language barriers, and local customs often prevent people from utilizing services. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T3#BMP323_U1_T3_h1)

question: Who should a midwifery team visit first when entering a new community for outreach?

options.A: Only the youngest children in the village
options.B: Traditional and local leadership figures
options.C: The nearest urban pharmaceutical store
options.D: International donors visiting from abroad

explanation: Visiting village heads and community leaders first shows respect and secures permission and cooperation for the health outreach. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T3#BMP323_U1_T3_h2)

question: A team of midwives arrives in a remote village without prior notice, and the residents refuse to bring their babies out for immunization. What vital step was missed?

options.A: Ordering more vaccines from the zonal cold store
options.B: Proper community entry and stakeholder sensitization
options.C: Changing the nursing uniform to casual clothes
options.D: Conducting a laboratory blood test on the village head

explanation: Failing to engage community leaders beforehand breeds suspicion and leads to low community participation. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T3#BMP323_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the main benefit of offering an integrated package during a community outreach?

options.A: It provides multiple health services at the same time
options.B: It guarantees free housing for the outreach team
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any fixed clinics
options.D: It ensures that midwives never have to travel by road

explanation: Integration saves time and resources by addressing several health needs during a single visit instead of separate trips. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T3#BMP323_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why is family planning typically included in a comprehensive maternal and child health outreach package?

options.A: To support birth spacing and improve overall maternal wellbeing
options.B: To satisfy administrative paperwork requirements for donors
options.C: To replace routine immunization services entirely
options.D: To reduce the total population of children under five years

explanation: Including family planning helps women space their pregnancies safely, which lowers risks for both mothers and babies. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T3#BMP323_U1_T3_h3)

question: What is the correct temperature range for storing routine vaccines in a cold box during outreach?

options.D: +2°C to +8°C

question: Why is accurate target population estimation crucial before packing supplies for an outreach trip?

options.A: It allows the midwife to predict exact weather patterns
options.B: It determines the exact vehicle speed needed on dirt roads
options.C: It stops community members from asking questions about care
options.D: It prevents running out of essential drugs or causing massive wastage

explanation: Knowing the approximate number of women and children expected helps the team bring enough supplies without carrying unnecessary excess weight. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T3#BMP323_U1_T3_h4)

question: Which method is commonly used by local mobilizers to spread news about an upcoming health outreach?

options.A: Publishing articles in national academic journals
options.B: Posting advertisements on commercial airline tickets
options.C: Town announcers using local dialects
options.D: Sending official letters to international embassies

explanation: Town announcers speaking the local language effectively reach households in rural and hard-to-reach Nigerian communities. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T3#BMP323_U1_T3_h5)

question: What happens when respected community leaders publicly participate in an outreach activity?

options.A: It removes the need for any vaccine cold chain equipment
options.B: It builds trust and encourages hesitant residents to come forward
options.C: It guarantees that funding will increase for the next year
options.D: It forces the health workers to finish their duties much faster

explanation: When leaders show support by example, community members feel safer and more confident in accepting the health services. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T3#BMP323_U1_T3_h5)

question: When should a midwife record data during an outreach service?

options.A: At the end of the entire month from memory
options.B: Immediately as each service is rendered
options.C: After returning home at the end of the week
options.D: Only if a supervisor visits the outreach site

explanation: Recording services immediately prevents forgetting details and ensures accurate health management information system data. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T3#BMP323_U1_T3_h6)

question: A midwife identifies a pregnant woman with severe pre-eclampsia during a remote outreach. What action must be taken alongside basic treatment?

options.A: Provide general nutrition counseling and tell her not to worry
options.B: Write a clear referral note and arrange safe transport to a higher facility
options.C: Wait until the next scheduled outreach month to check her again
options.D: Ask the woman to walk back to her home and rest for three days

explanation: Severe conditions require prompt stabilization, a written referral note, and active coordination of transport to a facility capable of managing emergencies. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T3#BMP323_U1_T3_h6)

question: Which national system collects the community health records that midwives gather in Nigeria?

options.A: West African Health Community Database
options.B: Nigerian Medical Association Statistical Board
options.C: National Health Management Information System
options.D: National Primary Health Care Development Agency

question: Why is recording routine health data considered an important task for a midwife?

options.A: It replaces the need to write patient notes in clinical folders
options.B: It turns individual patient visits into useful public health records
options.C: It ensures international visitors can audit the primary health centre
options.D: It is primarily required to calculate monthly salary disbursements

explanation: Routine data collection connects individual patient care with community-wide health tracking. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T4#BMP323_U1_T4_h1)

question: How is the Maternal Mortality Ratio typically reported in Nigeria?

options.A: Deaths per 100,000 live births
options.B: Deaths per 1,000 live births
options.C: Deaths per 1,000 total pregnancies
options.D: Deaths per 10,000 women of childbearing age

question: What does a high immunization dropout rate in a health clinic suggest?

options.A: Excessive community demand for routine antenatal care services
options.B: An immediate surplus of vaccine vials stored in the cold chain
options.C: A high rate of successful home deliveries without midwives
options.D: Poor tracking and follow-up for infants after their first visit

question: Which register should a midwife use to record labor progress and delivery outcomes?

options.C: Child Health Immunization Register
options.D: Daily Attendance Summary Sheet

question: After attending to a woman who just delivered a healthy baby boy, where must the midwife document this birth first?

options.A: Monthly summary notification form
options.B: Maternity Register (HMIS 012)
options.C: Local government immunization tally sheet
options.D: National DHIMS2 online portal

explanation: Documentation always begins at the bedside in the appropriate facility register before summary and electronic entry. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T4#BMP323_U1_T4_h3)

question: What does the acronym DHIMS2 stand for in the context of Nigerian health records?

question: Why are validation checks run inside the DHIMS2 platform before final report submission?

options.A: To automatically calculate monthly salary bonuses for clinical staff members

question: What is a common result of chronic reporting errors and inaccurate data from a primary health centre?

options.A: Immediate closure of the facility by international health inspectors

options.C: Automatic promotion of the midwife in charge of records
options.D: Doubling of patient attendance numbers in the following month

explanation: Poor data leads to incorrect supply estimates, which causes the government to send the wrong quantities of drugs and commodities. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T4#BMP323_U1_T4_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended way to prevent data reporting errors in a health facility?

options.A: Submitting reports months late to allow for relaxed review
options.B: Collecting tally sheets immediately after mobile outreach clinics
options.C: Cross-checking tally totals with a colleague before transcription
options.D: Verifying client attendance cards to avoid double counting

explanation: Late submissions delay the national information chain, so reports must always be submitted promptly by the required deadline. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T4#BMP323_U1_T4_h5)

question: A midwife notices that postnatal clinic attendance drops every July during heavy rains. What is the best local action to take?

options.A: Penalize mothers who miss their scheduled visits during the wet months

options.C: Collaborate with community leaders to organize flexible clinic hours or closer outreach points
options.D: Stop keeping postnatal records until the rainy season ends

question: How does analyzing local health data change the role of a primary care midwife?

options.A: It turns the midwife from a passive record-keeper into an active community health planner
options.B: It removes the need to submit monthly summary sheets to the local government
options.C: It allows the midwife to create medical supply budgets independently

explanation: Reviewing facility data helps solve local health challenges rather than just completing paperwork for outsiders. [learn more](BMP323_U1_T4#BMP323_U1_T4_h6)
